text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria sealed its first bank privatisation deal, selling 99.6 percent of United Bulgarian Bank to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Bulgaria's Bulbank and U.S. Oppenheimer & Co. Inc, for a total of $48 million, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Visiting President of Germany's Bundestag Rita Suessmuth said Germany backed Bulgaria's efforts to acquire European Union membership.
-- Bulgaria's agriculture ministry said the country had harvested 1.453 million tonnes of wheat so far from 36.35 of the wheat-sown area.

-- The Sofia City prosecutor Nestor Nestorov said the prosecution had launched an investigation against the former executive director of the state fund 13 Centuries Bulgaria Svetlana Sharenkova on suspicion of siphoning 300-400 million levs from the fund.
-- Bulgaria is planning to speed up privatisation of its Black Sea coast holiday resort hotels from September, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said.
-- Bulgaria's Prime minister Ivan Kostov said Bulgaria may seek to restructure the joint Bulgarian-Russian firm Topenergy or to set up a new joint firm to deliver Russian natural gas to Bulgaria.
-- Bulgaria retail prices rose by 1.7 percent in the past 10 days, the National Statistics Institute figures showed.
-- The Sofia City court said it had declared insolvent the state-owned Economic Bank on the basis of a claim filed by the Bulgarian National Bank.
-- Bulgaria's 1997 tobacco output is seen at 80,000 tonnes, up from 39,790 tonnes last year, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest state refinery Neftochim said it may raise petrol and diesel fuel prices by 10 percent from August 1, because of the dollar rise on international markets. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 91188
